items.title: Emad Mostaque claims physics axioms derived from one axiom, proved in Lean
items.takeaway: His claim, not independently checked: quantum mechanics and special relativity from the dot product, in 4 pages.
items.soWhat: AI-assisted formal proofs keep arriving; treat bold claims as unverified until experts check them.

items.title: Amjad Masad: Gemini 4 is now available in Replit
items.takeaway: Replit's CEO says Google really cooked with Gemini 4 and invites users to try it.
items.soWhat: Build platforms add new models within days; your teams can test alternatives without new contracts.

items.title: Claude read a 1994 Jeep's engine computer and found the smog fault
items.takeaway: Shared by Greg Isenberg: a $3 chip, about $15 in parts, code free on GitHub; the pass is self-reported.
items.soWhat: Cheap hardware plus an agent turns expert diagnostics into a weekend project.

items.title: Tavi Costa: gold miners now outperform the metal despite a correction
items.takeaway: The miners-to-gold ratio fell steadily in the bear market after the 2011 peak; that trend has turned.
items.soWhat: A long-running pattern in real assets may be reversing, a view worth tracking beyond AI.

items.title: Sam Altman credits Ven as early believer in AI on Millennium problems
items.takeaway: Altman says Ven believed early that the then-current model could be used on millennium prize problems.
items.soWhat: OpenAI's leader is pointing at frontier math as a proof point for its models.

items.title: swyx: decade-old SaaS founders are being forced to refound their companies
items.takeaway: He says this is forcing a reckoning with lazy lock-in business models.
items.soWhat: If AI makes switching cheap, revenue built on lock-in is at risk; audit yours.

items.title: Simon Willison writes up sqlite3_rsync for copying SQLite databases
items.takeaway: A remote-copy tool for SQLite databases.
items.soWhat: Simple tools for moving local data help teams run small agent apps without heavy infrastructure.
